notes.1: Many candidates appreciated that the release of energy from nutrient molecules is respiration. Some candidates incorrectly selected nutrition.
notes.2: Many candidates understood that in the binomial system the first name is the genus. Some candidates incorrectly believed that it is the second name that represents the genus.
notes.3: Many candidates were able to use the key to identify the organism as a crustacean. Some candidates incorrectly identified it as a myriapod. It is important that candidates methodically work through the key to determine the correct answer.
notes.4: A few candidates selected the correct option. The labelled structures that would also be found in an animal cell are W (the nucleus) and X (the cell membrane). Some candidates incorrectly opted for Z (the cell wall).
notes.6: Many candidates demonstrated an understanding of the magnification formula. Not all were able to convert cm to mm, with some multiplying by 1000 instead of 10.
notes.7: Most candidates appreciated that chemicals spread through the air by diffusion. Some candidates opted for active transport and transpiration.
notes.8: Some candidates correctly selected option B , the cell membrane. Other candidates opted for the cell wall, chloroplast, or vacuole.
notes.9: Very few candidates appreciated that both starch and glycogen are made of glucose molecules.
notes.11: Few candidates understood that the food tests indicated that protein and sugar were present.
notes.12: Few candidates understood that oxygen is the product of photosynthesis that moves out of a green leaf through its stomata.
notes.13: While many candidates appreciated that the factor the student investigated was light, a significant number of candidates incorrectly opted for chlorophyll.
notes.14: There was some uncertainty about this question with only a minority of candidates knowing that the nutrient required to prevent scurvy is vitamin C.
notes.15: Only a small proportion of candidates understood that diagram B represents the action of lipase.
notes.16: Many candidates were able to both identify and correctly measure the small intestine from the diagram. Some candidates incorrectly included the large intestine.
notes.17: Many candidates were able to identify the xylem in the cross-section of part of a leaf. Some candidates incorrectly opted for the palisade mesophyll cells.
notes.18: Only a minority of candidates understood which cells water must pass through to reach the xylem. Some candidates incorrectly believed that water must enter the phloem before reaching the xylem.
notes.20: Many candidates understood that blood clotting is slower than normal in a person with very few platelets. Some candidates incorrectly believed that antibody formation would be slower than normal.
notes.24: Very few candidates appeared familiar with the percentage composition of oxygen (16%) and carbon dioxide (4%) in expired air.
notes.25: Few candidates were able to correctly identify the ureter and the bladder from the diagram.
notes.26: Many candidates were able to correctly identify the conditions that will result in the largest volume of urine being produced by the kidneys. Some candidates did not appreciate that at higher temperatures, perspiration increases which decreases the volume of urine.
notes.28: Many candidates incorrectly believed that the pupil focuses light onto the retina.
notes.34: Only a small proportion of candidates understood that both the egg cell and the sperm must have an X chromosome to produce a female child.
notes.35: While many candidates appreciated that selective breeding involves parents that possess desirable features, some candidates incorrectly believed that it involves a struggle for survival.
notes.36: Many candidates understood that photosynthesis is the process that uses the principal source of energy input to biological systems. Some candidates incorrectly opted for respiration.
notes.38: Many candidates were unfamiliar with the definition of a population and could not apply it to the context in the question.
notes.40: Many candidates correctly selected option A . However, some candidates could not use the food web to determine the effect of chaffinches dying.
